mainTopic: Does a forbidden act take effect? אביי and רבא tested against תמורה, בכור, מעשר, תרומה, a widow and a כהן גדול, and blemished animals
overview: אביי and רבא argue about a general rule: when the תורה forbids an act and someone does it anyway, does the act still take effect? אביי says it does, and רבא says it does not. The גמרא tests both views against a series of cases. Against רבא it brings תמורה, תרומה separated before ביכורים, a widow who marries a כהן גדול, and consecrating blemished animals for the מזבח. Each of these works even though it is forbidden. Against אביי it brings בכור and מעשר, which cannot be redeemed even though redemption is only forbidden. Each time, the side under attack answers that the case is an exception learned from a special פסוק. The other side then shows what it learns from that same פסוק. Along the way the גמרא discusses blood of offerings that got mixed, and a לוי who took his מעשר early from the pile. The amud ends as the גמרא opens a new challenge about consecrating unblemished animals for בדק הבית, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: For רבא, the word 'הוא' excludes a firstborn from the ban on selling
steps.stepSummary: According to רבא, the word 'הוא' teaches that the ban on selling applies to מעשר and not to בכור. A ברייתא supports this: a בכור may not be redeemed but may be sold, while מעשר may never be sold in any state.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבא, this word 'הוא' comes to exclude a firstborn. As a ברייתא teaches: about a firstborn the תורה says 'you shall not redeem,' but it may be sold. About the animal tithe the תורה says 'it shall not be redeemed,' and it may not be sold. Not when alive and not when slaughtered, not when unblemished and not when blemished.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבא uses the word 'הוא' from the verse it was just discussing. For him it teaches that a בכור is different from מעשר when it comes to selling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא holds that a forbidden act never works anyway. So he does not need 'הוא' to teach that this act fails, and the word is free to teach something else. He uses it to set apart בכור: it may be sold, while מעשר may never be sold, no matter its condition.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn male kosher animal, which is holy from birth and given to the כהן
Here, the animal tithe: every tenth animal of the herd, which becomes holy
To exclude; a word in the פסוק comes to leave a case out of the rule
Unblemished, perfect animal
An animal with a blemish, which cannot be brought on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'redeeming' and 'selling.' Both בכור and מעשר cannot be redeemed. The difference is only about selling: a בכור may be sold, but מעשר may not.

steps.terutzMaskana: For רבא, 'הוא' excludes בכור from the ban on selling.

steps.title: Challenge to רבא from substituting an animal
steps.stepSummary: The תורה forbids תמורה, yet the משנה says the substitution takes effect and the person gets lashes. That shows a forbidden act does work, which goes against רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about substitution? The Merciful One says: 'He shall not exchange it, nor substitute it.' And the משנה teaches: it is not that a person is allowed to substitute. Rather, if he did substitute, the substitution takes effect, and he receives the forty lashes. So we see the act works. This is a refutation of רבא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's rule using the case of תמורה. It is forbidden, yet it still works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא says a forbidden act does not take effect. But with תמורה the act is both forbidden (he gets lashes) and effective (the new animal becomes holy). That looks like a direct contradiction of רבא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Substitution: trying to swap a regular animal for one that is already holy
Here: the substitution takes effect and the new animal becomes holy
He receives the forty lashes (in practice thirty-nine) for breaking a לא תעשה
So we see; this introduces a conclusion drawn from the source
A strong refutation, an objection that seems to knock down a view

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'מומר' does not mean a sinner who abandons Judaism. It means 'the swap has taken effect.'

phrases.english: But what about substitution,

"He shall not exchange it, nor substitute it,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:10

phrases.english: and it is taught:

phrases.english: It is not that a person is permitted to substitute,

So we see that it is effective,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from explaining רבא to challenging him with a new case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that a forbidden act does not take effect
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תמורה is forbidden, yet the משנה says it works. That is a case of a forbidden act taking effect.

steps.title: רבא answers: תמורה is different because a פסוק says so
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that תמורה is an exception. The פסוק explicitly says that both the original animal and its substitute are holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא can say to you: it is different there, because the פסוק says, 'Both it and its substitute shall be holy.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends himself. He says תמורה is a special case, because the תורה openly tells us the swap works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's general rule stays in place. Normally a forbidden act does not work, but here the תורה makes an exception in clear words. So תמורה does not prove anything against his rule; it only proves this one case is different.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there; the case being cited is special
'Both it and its substitute shall be holy': the פסוק that says the substitution works

steps.whatToRemember: For רבא, תמורה works only because the פסוק says so outright. It is an exception, not proof against his rule.

phrases.english: He can say to you:
phrases.notes: 'He' means רבא, answering the challenge.

phrases.english: It is different there,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר קְרָא ״וְהָיָה הוּא וּתְמוּרָתוֹ יִהְיֶה קֹּדֶשׁ״.
phrases.english: as the verse says: "Both it and its substitute shall be holy."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:10, the same פסוק that forbids the swap.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from תמורה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: תמורה seemed to prove that forbidden acts take effect in general.
steps.terutzMaskana: תמורה takes effect only because of a special פסוק, so רבא's general rule still stands.

steps.title: Why אביי still needs the פסוק 'both it and its substitute'
steps.stepSummary: For אביי, forbidden acts work anyway, so the פסוק seems unneeded. The גמרא explains that without it we might think the holiness moves from the first animal to the second. The פסוק teaches that both stay holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to אביי: if the Merciful One had not said 'both it and its substitute,' I would have said that this one leaves and that one enters. So the פסוק teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the פסוק teaches according to אביי. He does not need it to show that the swap works, so it must teach something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי already knows the swap works, because for him forbidden acts take effect. But 'working' could have meant a full trade, where the holiness moves to the new animal and the old one becomes ordinary. The words 'it and its substitute' teach that both animals are holy.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought; the mistaken idea we would have without the source
This one leaves and that one enters: the holiness would move from one animal to the other
It teaches us; the source comes to rule out the mistaken idea

steps.whatToRemember: Both אביי and רבא use the פסוק 'הוא ותמורתו' but for different lessons. For רבא, it shows the swap works at all. For אביי, it shows that both animals remain holy.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the halacha of תמורה: the original animal keeps its holiness, and the substitute becomes holy too.

phrases.english: And according to Abaye,
if the Merciful One had not said
"both it and its substitute,"
I would have said

phrases.notes: Meaning the holy animal would become ordinary, and the new animal would take its holiness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After using the פסוק for רבא, the גמרא explains why אביי also needs it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds a different lesson in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The swap works by moving the holiness from the first animal to the second.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both the original animal and the substitute are holy.

steps.title: The firstborn case seems to refute אביי
steps.stepSummary: The תורה says not to redeem a בכור, and the משנה says a בכור cannot be redeemed. So a forbidden act does not work here, which looks like a full refutation of אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about a בכור? The תורה says 'you shall not redeem' it. And a משנה teaches that holy animals can be redeemed, and so can their substitutes, except for the בכור and the מעשר. So it seems that redeeming a בכור does not work. That is a refutation of אביי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי with a case where the תורה forbids something and the act clearly does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי holds that even when the תורה forbids an act, the act still takes effect. But a בכור is forbidden to be redeemed, and the משנה says redemption does not apply to it at all. That fits רבא's view, so it looks like a תיובתא against אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn male animal, which is holy from birth
Redemption: taking away an animal's holiness by exchanging it for money
Apparently / this shows that
It does not take effect
A strong refutation of an opinion

phrases.english: But what about a firstborn,
about which the Merciful One said, 'You shall not redeem,'
phrases.notes: במדבר יח:יז

phrases.english: and we learned in a משנה: they can be redeemed,

phrases.english: and their substitutes can be redeemed,
except for the firstborn and the tithe animal.
Apparently, it does not take effect,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the תמורה challenge against רבא was answered and אביי's reading of that פסוק was explained, the גמרא brings a new case against אביי.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's view that a forbidden act still takes effect
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redeeming a בכור is forbidden, and the משנה says it does not work. So a forbidden act failed to take effect.

steps.title: אביי: the word 'הם' makes the firstborn different
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the same פסוק says 'הם' (they are holy). This teaches that a בכור always stays as it is, so the case is an exception.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי can answer you: it is different there, because the פסוק says 'they are' holy. That means they stay in their state.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends himself by saying the בכור is a special case with its own פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, in אביי's view, a forbidden act still works. But by בכור, the extra word 'הם' tells us the animal stays holy no matter what, so redemption cannot work here. The general rule stands, and the בכור is an exception.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there; that case is special
They shall stay as they are

phrases.english: He could say to you: it is different there,
because the פסוק says 'they are,'
phrases.notes: This is the end of the same פסוק: 'you shall not redeem; they are holy.'

phrases.english: meaning they shall stay as they are.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from בכור.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Exception from a special word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The בכור case proves that forbidden acts never work.
steps.terutzMaskana: The בכור is an exception because 'הם' says it stays holy. The general rule of אביי is not touched.

steps.title: What does רבא learn from 'הם'?
steps.stepSummary: For רבא, forbidden acts never work anyway, so redemption of a בכור fails without any extra word. So why does the פסוק need to say 'הם'?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבא, why does he need this word 'הם'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבא and asks what the word 'הם' adds for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא already holds that a forbidden act does not take effect, so he does not need 'הם' to tell him a בכור stays holy. The גמרא wants to know what extra lesson 'הם' teaches for him.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does he need it? (asking what a word adds)

phrases.english: And according to רבא, why does he need this 'they are'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Once 'הם' is used by אביי, the גמרא asks how the other side uses it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word 'הם' teaches according to רבא

steps.title: For רבא, 'הם' means only the originals are offered
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from 'הם' that the original בכור and מעשר animals are offered on the מזבח, but their substitutes are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are offered, but their substitutes are not offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבא uses 'הם' to teach a different law: only the original animals go on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'הם' means 'they', the originals and not anything else. So if someone made a תמורה for a בכור or מעשר, the substitute is holy but is not brought as a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Are offered as a קרבן on the מזבח
Their substitutes, animals swapped in place of them

steps.confusionAlert: The substitute is still holy. It just is not offered. Do not think 'not offered' means 'not holy'.

phrases.english: They are offered,
but their substitutes are not offered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'הם' teaches that only the original animals are offered, not their substitutes.

steps.title: Where does אביי learn that substitutes are not offered?
steps.stepSummary: אביי used 'הם' for a different lesson, so the גמרא asks where he gets the rule that substitutes are not offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to אביי, where does he get this idea?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for אביי's source for the rule that רבא learned from 'הם'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי already used 'הם' to teach that a בכור stays holy and cannot be redeemed. So the word is taken, and he needs a different source for the rule that substitutes are not offered.

keyTerms.meaning: Idea / rule (here, the law that substitutes are not offered)
From where does he learn it?

phrases.english: And according to אביי, from where does he get this idea?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After hearing רבא's use of 'הם', the גמרא asks how אביי gets the same law.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: אביי's source that substitutes of בכור are not offered

steps.title: אביי learns it from 'לה׳ הוא'
steps.stepSummary: אביי learns it from the פסוק 'whether ox or sheep, it is the Lord's'. 'It' is offered to ה׳, but its substitute is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'Whether ox or sheep, it is the Lord's.' It is offered to ה׳, but its substitute is not offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives אביי a different פסוק as the source for the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'הוא' ('it') limits the offering to the בכור itself. So both אביי and רבא agree on the law that substitutes are not offered. They only disagree about which word teaches it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is the Lord's': the word 'it' points to the original animal only
Is offered

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree that a substitute of a בכור is holy but not offered. אביי learns it from 'לה׳ הוא', because he needs 'הם' to teach that a בכור cannot be redeemed. The next step shows that רבא learns it from 'לה׳ הוא' too.

phrases.english: 'Whether ox or sheep, it is the Lord's':
phrases.notes: ויקרא כז:כו

phrases.english: to ה׳ it is offered,
but its substitute is not offered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9. Step 11 then asks how רבא uses this same פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אביי learns from 'לה׳ הוא' that only the בכור itself is offered, not its substitute.

steps.title: רבא also learns the substitute rule from the ox-or-sheep verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבא does with the ox-or-sheep פסוק. It answers that he agrees with אביי and learns from it that substitutes are not offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא? Yes, it is indeed so: he too learns it from that verse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבא uses the פסוק that אביי used in step 10. It answers that רבא learns the same thing from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 8, רבא learned from 'הם' that substitutes are not offered. Now the גמרא says רבא can learn that rule from 'הוא' in the ox-or-sheep פסוק, just like אביי. This leaves the word 'הם' free for רבא to use for something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, that is indeed so (agreeing with the suggestion)
A verse (פסוק)

phrases.english: And Rava?
phrases.notes: The question is short: what does רבא do with the ox-or-sheep פסוק from step 10?

phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so, that it is from that verse.
phrases.notes: רבא also learns that substitutes are not offered from this same פסוק (ויקרא 27:26).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא, אִין הָכִי נָמֵי דְּמֵהָהוּא קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies אביי's source from step 10 to רבא as well.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבא agrees that the ox-or-sheep פסוק teaches that substitutes are not offered.

steps.title: Then what is the word 'הם' for, according to רבא?
steps.stepSummary: If רבא learns the substitute rule from 'הוא', what does the word 'הם' teach him?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then why do I need 'הם'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the extra word 'הם' teaches רבא, now that he learns the substitute rule from a different פסוק. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes no word in the תורה is extra. In step 7 'הם' was not needed for redemption according to רבא, and now it is not needed for substitutes either. So the word must teach something new.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? (asking what a word is there to teach)

phrases.english: But why do I need "they are"?
phrases.notes: This is the word 'הם' in במדבר 18:17, 'they are holy'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 11, since 'הם' is now free.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new rule does 'הם' teach according to רבא?

steps.title: 'הם' teaches that mixed blood of בכור and מעשר is still offered
steps.stepSummary: According to רבא, 'הם' teaches that if blood of a בכור or מעשר mixes with blood of other offerings, it is still put on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches that a בכור or מעשר whose blood got mixed with the blood of any offering brought on the מזבח is still offered on the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבא's new lesson from 'הם'. Mixed blood of these animals is not cancelled and is still offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think blood mixed into a larger amount of other blood loses its identity and is cancelled. 'הם' teaches that these animals stay 'as they are' even inside a mixture. So the blood still goes on the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: Got mixed
Their blood
Things that are brought up onto the altar

phrases.english: It teaches about a firstborn and a tithe animal
whose blood got mixed
with the blood of any offerings that go up
phrases.notes: Any other offering whose blood goes on the מזבח.

phrases.english: that it is offered on the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִימֵּד עַל בְּכוֹר וּמַעֲשֵׂר שֶׁנִּתְעָרֵב דָּמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'הם' teaches that בכור and מעשר blood mixed with other blood is not cancelled and is still offered.

steps.title: Where does אביי learn the rule about mixed blood?
steps.stepSummary: אביי used 'הם' for something else, so where does he get the rule that mixed blood is still offered?
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי, where does he get this idea from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for אביי's source for the mixed-blood rule. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6, אביי used 'הם' to teach that a בכור stays as it is and cannot be redeemed. So 'הם' is not available to him for the blood-mixture rule. He needs another source.

keyTerms.meaning: An idea or line of reasoning (here, the mixed-blood rule)
From where does he know it?

phrases.english: And Abaye, where does he get this idea from?
phrases.notes: 'This idea' is the rule from step 13, that mixed blood is still offered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Checks whether אביי can also arrive at רבא's rule from step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: אביי's source for the rule that mixed blood is not cancelled.

steps.title: אביי learns it from the bull and goat blood of יום כיפור
steps.stepSummary: On יום כיפור the כהן גדול puts mixed bull and goat blood on the מזבח. The goat blood is not cancelled even though there is less of it, so offerings do not cancel each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the פסוק 'And he shall take of the blood of the bull and of the blood of the goat.' But isn't there more bull blood than goat blood? From here we learn that offerings do not cancel each other. As a ברייתא teaches: 'And he shall take of the blood of the bull and of the blood of the goat' means they must be mixed. These are the words of רבי יאשיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows אביי's source: the יום כיפור blood. The goat blood stays valid even though the bull blood is bigger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא of רבי יאשיה reads the פסוק as requiring the two bloods to be mixed. Even so, the smaller amount of goat blood still counts. This shows that blood of offerings does not cancel other blood of offerings, so אביי has the rule without needing 'הם'.

keyTerms.meaning: Larger in amount
Cancel out (a smaller amount losing its identity in a larger one)
Mixed together

phrases.english: From "And he shall take of the blood of the bull
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:18, about the כהן גדול on יום כיפור.

phrases.english: and of the blood of the goat."
But isn't the bull's blood
more than the goat's?
From here we learn that things that go up on the altar
do not cancel each other out,
as a ברייתא teaches:
"And he shall take of the blood of the bull and of the blood of the goat"
means that they must be mixed together.
These are the words of Rabbi Yoshiya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 with a different פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אביי learns the rule from the mixed bull and goat blood of יום כיפור, following רבי יאשיה.

steps.title: רבא reads the יום כיפור blood as applied separately
steps.stepSummary: רבא does not learn from the יום כיפור blood, because he holds like רבי יונתן that each blood was applied by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא? There, the כהן גדול takes from this blood by itself and from that blood by itself. He holds like רבי יונתן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבא does not use אביי's source. In his view the bloods were never mixed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the bull and goat blood were applied separately, nothing was mixed and nothing could be cancelled. Then the פסוק proves nothing about mixtures. So רבא needs 'הם' as his source, while אביי follows רבי יאשיה.

keyTerms.meaning: By itself, separately
He holds like (the opinion of)

phrases.english: And Rava? There,
he puts from this one by itself
and from that one by itself,
and he holds like Rabbi Yonatan.
phrases.notes: רבי יונתן is the one who argues with רבי יאשיה and says the bloods are not mixed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא, הָתָם — מִזֶּה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ וּמִזֶּה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבא does not accept the source from step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the יום כיפור blood as a proof for רבא only.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: According to רבי יונתן the bloods are applied separately, so there is no mixture to learn from.
steps.whatToRemember: Both agree that mixed blood is offered. רבא learns it from 'הם'. אביי learns it from the יום כיפור blood, following רבי יאשיה, since he used 'הם' for the בכור rule.

steps.title: Challenge to אביי: a מעשר animal cannot be redeemed
steps.stepSummary: The תורה says a מעשר animal 'shall not be redeemed', and a משנה says redemption does not work on it. This suggests a forbidden act does not work, against אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about מעשר, about which the Merciful One says 'it shall not be redeemed'? And we learned in a משנה: they and their substitutes can be redeemed, except for the בכור and the מעשר. This shows that redeeming it does not work. This is a refutation of אביי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a strong challenge to אביי from the case of מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי holds that a forbidden act still works. For בכור he had the word 'הם' to explain the exception, but the מעשר פסוק has no such word. Yet the משנה says redeeming מעשר fails, which fits רבא's view that a forbidden act does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: It shall not be redeemed
Redemption (taking away the holiness for money)
This shows that
A strong refutation

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the end of the discussion. In the גמרא, 'תיובתא' here opens a challenge that is answered in the lines that follow.

phrases.english: But what about a tithe animal,
about which the Merciful One says, "It shall not be redeemed"?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:33

phrases.english: And we learned in a משנה: they can be redeemed
and so can their substitutes,
except for the firstborn and the tithe animal.
This shows it does not work,
a refutation of Abaye.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the main argument between אביי and רבא after the side discussion about blood mixtures.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's view that a forbidden act still works.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מעשר פסוק forbids redemption and has no 'הם' to make it an exception. Since the משנה says redemption fails, a forbidden act seems not to work.
steps.whyThisMatters: This brings the debate back to its core question: does an act the תורה forbids still take effect?

steps.title: אביי: the מעשר case is special because it is learned from בכור
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that מעשר בהמה cannot be redeemed only because of a גזירה שוה from בכור, so it says nothing about forbidden acts in general.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי can tell you: that case is different, because we learn it from בכור through the matching word 'עברה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge against אביי from Step 17. It says the מעשר case is a special rule, not a general principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was that redeeming מעשר does not work even though it is forbidden. אביי replies that this comes from a גזירה שוה linking מעשר to בכור, and a בכור can never be redeemed. So it is a special exception, and in general אביי still holds that a forbidden act does work.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there; that case is special
Learning one law from another because the תורה uses the same word in both places
'Passing', the shared word used for both מעשר and בכור
Firstborn animal, which is holy from birth

phrases.english: He [אביי] will tell you: it is different there,
because one learns 'passing' and 'passing' from a firstborn.
phrases.notes: מעשר uses 'whatever passes under the rod' (ויקרא 27:32), and בכור uses 'you shall set apart [והעברת]' (שמות 13:12).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא against אביי from Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: it is a special exception learned through a גזירה שוה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מעשר case seemed to show that every forbidden act fails to work.
steps.terutzMaskana: The failure of redemption for מעשר comes from בכור, so it does not show a general rule.

steps.title: Challenge to רבא: תרומה separated before ביכורים still counts
steps.stepSummary: Separating תרומה before ביכורים is forbidden, yet a משנה says it still works. This goes against רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about someone who separated תרומה before ביכורים? The תורה says 'Do not delay your full produce and your juice,' and a משנה teaches that if someone does it first, even though he broke a לא תעשה, what he did is done.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא turns and attacks רבא's view that a forbidden act does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק teaches that ביכורים must be taken before תרומה, so doing it the other way breaks a לאו. Even so, the משנה says the תרומה is real. That means a forbidden act worked, which goes against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to the כהן
First fruits brought to the מקדש
A negative commandment, a prohibition
What he did is done; the act takes effect

phrases.english: But there is one who put תרומה before the first fruits,
about which the Merciful One said: 'Your full produce and your juice, do not delay,'
phrases.notes: שמות 22:28. Earlier, on 4a, this was explained as giving the order: ביכורים first, then תרומה.

phrases.english: and we learned in a משנה: one who puts it first,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא בְּלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה —
phrases.english: even though he is breaking a prohibition,
what he did is done!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending אביי, the גמרא now challenges רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's view that a forbidden act does not take effect.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Separating תרומה before ביכורים is forbidden, yet the משנה rules that it works, so a forbidden act does take effect.

steps.title: רבא: a special פסוק teaches that תרומה always works
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that תרומה is special because the פסוק 'From all your tithes you shall separate תרומה' teaches that it works in any case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא can tell you: that case is different, because the פסוק says, 'From all your tithes you shall separate תרומה.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge by saying the תרומה case is a special exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא holds that a forbidden act normally does not work. The phrase 'from all' teaches that separating תרומה works in every situation, even when it was done in the wrong order. So this is a special פסוק, and it does not change the general rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Your tithes; the gifts you separate from produce
You shall separate (as a gift)
The פסוק, the verse

phrases.english: רבא will tell you: it is different there,
because the verse says: 'From all your tithes you shall separate תרומה.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:29. The words 'from all' are what tell us תרומה works in every situation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא against רבא from Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case through a special פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תרומה case seemed to prove that forbidden acts take effect.
steps.terutzMaskana: תרומה works only because of a special פסוק. In general, forbidden acts do not take effect according to רבא.

steps.title: What אביי learns from the פסוק: רב פפא's question
steps.stepSummary: אביי does not need the פסוק for תרומה that was separated early, so the גמרא explains he uses it for another rule. It starts quoting רב פפא's question to אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי needs the פסוק for something else, as רב פפא said to אביי: if that is so, then even if he took it first from the pile, it should also be exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what אביי uses the פסוק 'from all your tithes' for, since for him it is not needed to teach that תרומה works. It is setting up a quote, and the explanation continues after this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי a forbidden act works anyway, so the פסוק would teach nothing new about early תרומה. The גמרא points to רב פפא's challenge about a לוי who took his מעשר early from a pile of grain. Exempting that pile from תרומה makes no sense, so the פסוק is needed for that law instead.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for another teaching)
If that is so, then... (introduces a challenge that follows from what was said)
A pile of grain that has been threshed and gathered
He took it first, before his turn

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא's words here are a question he asked אביי in a different place. They are quoted here only to show which law the פסוק teaches according to אביי.

phrases.english: And for אביי, he needs it [the verse] for something else,
as רב פפא said to אביי:
If that is so,
phrases.notes: He is reacting to ריש לקיש's rule that a לוי who took מעשר ראשון early from the stalks doesn't have to give תרומה from it.

phrases.english: then even if he took it first from the pile, let it also be exempt!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא used the פסוק in Step 20, the גמרא explains what אביי uses that same פסוק for.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: If forbidden acts work anyway for אביי, what does he learn from 'from all your tithes'?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He needs it for the law behind רב פפא's question about מעשר that was taken early from the pile. The explanation continues after this line.

steps.title: אביי answers רב פפא with the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: אביי tells רב פפא that the פסוק 'מכל מעשרותיכם תרימו' covers his case. A לוי who took his מעשר from the pile still owes תרומה גדולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: About you, the verse says, 'From all your tithes you shall separate תרומה.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question רב פפא asked at the end of the last step. He points to the פסוק that uses the word 'all'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא wanted to say that a לוי who got his מעשר early from the pile should also be exempt from תרומה גדולה. אביי says the word 'all' in the פסוק includes that case. So the לוי must still separate תרומה גדולה. This is the use אביי has for the פסוק, since he does not need it to teach that early תרומה works.

keyTerms.meaning: Your tithes. Here it means the מעשר ראשון the לויים receive.
You shall separate (a portion as תרומה).
The main תרומה given to the כהן before the tithes are taken.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: אביי is answering רב פפא.

phrases.english: About you the verse says:
"From all your tithes you shall separate."
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:29

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's question that began in step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'all' in the פסוק requires תרומה גדולה even from מעשר taken early from the pile.

steps.title: Why include the pile and not the stalks?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks how אביי knows the word 'all' includes the pile but not the stalks.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did you see to include the pile and to leave out the stalks?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא asks a follow-up question. If 'all' includes something, why does it include the pile and not the stalks too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know a לוי who took his מעשר from the stalks is exempt from תרומה גדולה. רב פפא wants to know the reason for the line between the two cases. Why does 'all' reach the pile but stop before the stalks?

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see? A way of asking for the reason behind a distinction.
A pile of grain that is already threshed and gathered.
Stalks. The grain while it is still on the stalk.

phrases.english: What did you see to include the pile
phrases.notes: Include it in the word 'all', so the לוי must give תרומה גדולה.

phrases.english: and to exclude the stalks?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the line אביי drew in step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The basis for including the pile in 'all' while leaving out the stalks.

steps.title: The pile counts as 'grain', the stalks do not
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that grain in a pile is called דגן, so it already owes תרומה. Stalks are not yet דגן.
steps.simpleTranslation: I include the pile, because it counts as 'grain'. I exclude the stalks, because they do not count as 'grain' yet.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains the line he drew. Once grain is piled up it is called 'דגן', and stalks are not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The duty of תרומה applies to 'דגנך', your grain. Grain in a pile is already finished and already owes תרומה, so a לוי who took from it cannot escape תרומה גדולה. Grain on the stalk does not owe תרומה yet, so taking from it early is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: Include, add in.
Exclude, leave out.
The category of 'grain' (דגן). Grain that is finished enough to owe תרומה.

steps.whatToRemember: A לוי who takes his מעשר from the pile, before תרומה is separated, still owes תרומה גדולה. One who takes it from the stalks does not. This is how אביי uses 'מכל מעשרותיכם'.

phrases.english: I include the pile,
because it is in the category of grain,
and I exclude the stalks,
because they are not in the category of grain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's question from step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The pile is already 'דגן' and owes תרומה. The stalks are not yet 'דגן'.

steps.title: A widow who marries a כהן גדול: the marriage works
steps.stepSummary: The תורה forbids a כהן גדול to marry a widow, yet a משנה says such קידושין work. This seems to go against רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about a widow with a כהן גדול? The תורה says 'a widow or a divorcee he shall not take.' Yet we learned: wherever there is קידושין and there is also a sin, the child follows the parent with the flaw.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the main argument and brings a new challenge against רבא. Here is a forbidden marriage that still takes effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא holds that when the תורה forbids an act, the act does not work. But a כהן גדול who marries a widow does something forbidden, and the משנה calls it 'קידושין with a sin'. That means the קידושין take effect. This fits אביי, who says a forbidden act still works.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow married to a כהן גדול, which the תורה forbids.
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage that takes legal effect.
A sin, a forbidden act.
The child follows the parent with the flawed status.

steps.confusionAlert: The proof is not about the child. It comes from the משנה's wording 'יש קידושין': the משנה calls the forbidden marriage real קידושין.

phrases.english: But what about a widow with a High Priest,
for the Merciful One said:
"A widow or a divorcee... he shall not take,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:14

phrases.english: and we learned: Any place where there is betrothal
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in קידושין 66b.

phrases.english: and there is a sin —
the child follows the flawed one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side point about אביי's use of the פסוק and returns to challenging רבא, as in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's view that a forbidden act does not take effect.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The marriage is forbidden by the תורה, yet the משנה says the קידושין take effect. So a forbidden act does work.

steps.title: A special פסוק: 'he shall not profane his seed'
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that this case is different, because the פסוק 'לא יחלל זרעו' shows the marriage takes effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it is different, because the verse says: 'He shall not profane his seed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבא. A special פסוק covers this case, so it does not prove a general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says only that the child becomes 'profaned' (a חלל). It does not say the child is a ממזר, which is what happens when קידושין cannot take effect. So we learn that this forbidden marriage does work. The reason is this special פסוק, while in general רבא still holds that forbidden acts do not work.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it is different. Used to show a case is an exception.
He shall not profane his offspring. The child becomes a חלל, not a ממזר.
A child of a forbidden כהן marriage who loses כהונה status.

steps.whyThisMatters: This follows the same pattern as step 20. When a forbidden act clearly works, רבא points to a special פסוק for that case, so his general rule still stands.

phrases.english: It is different here,
for the verse says:
"He shall not profane his seed."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:15. The child is only 'profaned', not a ממזר, so the marriage must have taken effect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רבא from step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special פסוק for this case only
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A widow's marriage to a כהן גדול shows that every forbidden act takes effect.
steps.terutzMaskana: The marriage works only because 'לא יחלל זרעו' teaches it. In general, a forbidden act does not work, as רבא holds.

steps.title: What אביי learns from the longer word 'לא יחלל'
steps.stepSummary: אביי does not need 'לא יחלל' to show that the marriage works. He learns from its longer form that there are two kinds of profaning, one for the child and one for the woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to אביי, the verse could have said 'לא יחל'. Why does it say 'לא יחלל'? To teach one for him and one for her.
steps.whatsHappening: In step 26, רבא used 'לא יחלל' to show the כהן גדול's marriage works. Now the גמרא asks what אביי, who does not need that proof, learns from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, a forbidden act works anyway, so the פסוק must teach something else. The shorter 'לא יחל' would have been enough, so the extra ל points to two profanations. The child becomes a חלל, and the woman becomes disqualified from כהונה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He shall not profane'. The longer form of the word, with a doubled ל
The shorter form of the same word, which the פסוק could have used
One for him (the child) and one for her (the woman). Two separate profanations

phrases.english: And according to Abaye, let the verse say 'lo yachel'.
Why does it say 'lo yechallel'?
One for him, and one for her.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the child, who becomes a חלל. 'Her' is the woman, who becomes unfit to marry any כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְאַבָּיֵי, נֵימָא קְרָא ״לֹא יַחֵל״, מַאי ״לֹא יְחַלֵּל״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא used the פסוק in step 26, the גמרא explains how אביי reads the same פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra ל in 'יחלל' teaches two profanations: one for the child and one for the woman.

steps.title: Challenge to רבא from consecrating blemished animals
steps.stepSummary: The תורה forbids offering blemished animals, yet a משנה says that if someone consecrates them for the מזבח, the הקדש takes effect. This seems to refute רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about someone who consecrated blemished animals for the מזבח? The תורה says, 'Anything with a blemish you shall not offer.' And we learned: one who consecrates blemished animals for the מזבח, even though he broke a prohibition, what he did is done. This is a refutation of רבא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case where the תורה forbids an act, but the act still takes effect. This seems to go against רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא says a forbidden act does not take effect. Here the person breaks a לא תעשה by consecrating a blemished animal, yet the source says 'what he did is done'. That looks like clear proof against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals with a blemish, which are unfit to be offered as קרבנות
One who consecrates something, making it holy (הקדש)
A negative commandment, a 'do not'
What he did is done. The act takes effect
A strong refutation

phrases.english: But what about one who consecrated blemished animals for the altar,
about which the Merciful One said:
'Anything that has a blemish you shall not offer'?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:20

phrases.aramaic: וּתְנַן: הַמַּקְדִּישׁ בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ,
phrases.english: And we learned: one who consecrates blemished animals for the altar,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא בְּלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה —
phrases.english: even though he has broken a prohibition,
what he did is done.
This is a refutation of Rava!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another challenge to רבא, built the same way as the תרומה challenge (step 19) and the כהן גדול and widow challenge (step 25).
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that a forbidden act does not take effect
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Consecrating a blemished animal breaks a לא תעשה, yet the הקדש works. So forbidden acts do take effect.

steps.title: רבא: a special פסוק shows this הקדש works
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that blemished animals are a special case. The פסוק 'ולנדר לא ירצה' says only that the animal will not be accepted as a קרבן, which implies that it is still holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא can tell you: it is different there, because the verse says, 'But for a vow it shall not be accepted.' Only acceptance does not happen. But it does become holy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his view by saying the תורה itself shows that this particular case takes effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק takes away only one thing: the animal will not be accepted as a קרבן. By saying only that, it implies the הקדש itself does work. So this is an exception taught by a פסוק, and רבא's general rule still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there. Used to set a case apart as an exception
'But for a vow it shall not be accepted'
Acceptance of a קרבן, so that it is pleasing to ה׳
They do become holy

phrases.english: Rava can say to you:
It is different there, because the verse says:
'But for a vow it shall not be accepted.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:23

phrases.english: It is acceptance that it does not bring about,
which implies that they do become holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28, the same way רבא answered in step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special verse makes this case an exception
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a forbidden הקדש works here, forbidden acts work in general.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only here does the פסוק show that the הקדש works. In general, forbidden acts still do not take effect.

steps.title: What אביי learns from 'ולנדר לא ירצה'
steps.stepSummary: אביי does not need the פסוק to show the הקדש works. He learns from it that the blemished animal may not be offered, even after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to אביי: if the Merciful One had not said 'But for a vow it shall not be accepted,' I would have thought it is like one who broke a מצוה, but the animal is still fit. So the פסוק teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what אביי learns from the same פסוק that רבא just used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the פסוק, we might think the person did wrong, but once the animal is consecrated it may still be brought as a קרבן. The פסוק teaches that it is not accepted, so it cannot be offered.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought. The first assumption before the lesson is learned
One who broke a מצוה, but the result is still valid and fit
It teaches us. The פסוק comes to correct the first assumption

steps.whatToRemember: Both cases (the כהן גדול marrying a widow, and consecrating a blemished animal) work the same way. רבא calls each one an exception taught by a special פסוק. אביי, who holds that forbidden acts work anyway, uses the same פסוקים to learn a different lesson.

phrases.english: And according to Abaye: if the Merciful One had not said
'But for a vow it shall not be accepted,'
I would have said: it is like one who broke a מצוה, but it is still fit.
So it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְאַבָּיֵי, אִי דְּלָא אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא ״וּלְנֶדֶר לֹא יֵרָצֶה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Like step 27, it explains how אביי reads the פסוק that רבא used in the step before.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק teaches that a consecrated blemished animal may not be offered, even after the fact.

steps.title: A new challenge: consecrating unblemished animals for Temple upkeep
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens another challenge to רבא. It brings the case of someone who consecrates unblemished animals for בדק הבית, which the תורה forbids, and begins to quote the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is the case of someone who consecrates unblemished animals for Temple upkeep, about which the Merciful One says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge to רבא. It names the case and starts to quote the פסוק, which comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An unblemished animal is fit to be a קרבן on the מזבח, so the תורה does not want it given to בדק הבית instead. If that kind of הקדש still takes effect, then a forbidden act does work, which goes against רבא. The full challenge depends on the פסוק that the גמרא is about to quote.

keyTerms.meaning: One who consecrates (makes something holy)
Unblemished animals, fit to be brought as קרבנות
Temple upkeep fund, used for repairs, not for the מזבח
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the last case. Before, blemished animals were given to the מזבח. Now it is the opposite: unblemished animals are given to בדק הבית.

phrases.english: But there is one who consecrates unblemished animals
for Temple upkeep,
about which the Merciful One says:
phrases.notes: The פסוק itself comes on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the blemished-animal challenge was answered (steps 28-30), the גמרא brings a new case of a forbidden הקדש to test רבא again.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that anything the תורה forbids does not take effect if done
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Consecrating unblemished animals for בדק הבית is forbidden by a פסוק. If that הקדש still works, then a forbidden act does take effect, against רבא.
